the analysis of high-throughput omics data, with a focus on the integration of parallel data sets and their biological interpretation in the context of signaling networks.

the development of a new pathway-based approach to the analysis of coupled time-course data sets generated in parallel from different high-throughputs platforms and its application to a data set generated in the context of epidermal growth factors signaling in human mammary epithelia.

the new approach for the integrated analysis of omics data sets is able to identify new regulatory interactions in a signaling context.
the new approach is able to identify important interactions in signaling networks and thus is able to provide new insights into the dynamics of signaling processes.
our approach is able to identify and characterize important regulatory interactions and feedback signaling mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach allows to integrate different omics data sets and to infer regulatory mechanisms from them.

the combination of different high-throughput techniques with our new approach enables a better understanding of the dynamics of signaling mechanisms and thus facilitates the identification of potential therapeutic targets.
we developed a new approach for the analysis and interpretation of coupled high-throughput time-series data sets.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the integration of cross-platform time-course data sets is feasible and provides valuable information for the characterization and interpretation of regulatory mechanisms in complex signaling networks.

integrated cross-platform pathway-based analysis of omics time-series provides a deeper understanding for regulatory signaling mechanisms and enables the identification of dynamic signaling processes.
the integration of different omics layers can provide a deeper understanding of the regulatory mechanisms underlying signaling pathways.
